description: The R&D Tax Incentive can be a critical source of funding for Australian startups and innovative businesses. This session covers how the incentive works, who is eligible, and what the recent budget announcements change. It goes past filling in a claim to the practices that make one defensible: contemporaneous record-keeping, the documentation that substantiates a claim, and the habits that reduce audit risk. 2:45–3:35pm
venue: Clarence Workspaces for Lawyers, Level 21, 133 Castlereagh Street, Sydney

title: Build Something Useful With AI — Live
description: Bring a real problem. Michael Batko picks a couple of challenges from the room and builds the solution live - a website, an AI agent, a workflow - showing the thinking, the tools and the decisions as the work comes together. The value is as much in watching the approach as in the finished build. 3:00–5:00pm

title: Tech Central Walking Tour
description: A guided walk through Tech Central, Australia's largest innovation precinct, taking in the landmarks and facilities and what is being built there next. Tech Central — meet at UTS Tower concierge 4:00–4:50pm
venue: Tech Central — meet at UTS Tower concierge

title: Building With AI: What Changes at Every Stage
description: Martin Medina built Solotude as the only technical person on the team, using AI-assisted development. He shows how he actually works, where he lets agents run, where he reviews every line, and how much to trust AI changes as a product moves from prototype to something people rely on daily. 4:00–4:50pm

title: Vibe-Coded It. Now Make It Real.
description: You built something with AI and it works. Now comes the harder part: making it reliable, secure, scalable and ready for real customers. Mike Gardiner works with a small group on the last ten per cent between a promising prototype and something people can depend on - testing, reliability, security, usability. 5:00–9:00pm

title: Google Developer community event — AI
description: An evening for the Google developer community on AI at Google's Sydney office: a panel on AI and sovereignty, a walkthrough of building a secure, compliant agent with Antigravity and the Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, food and drinks, then a hands-on Vibe Coding Agent Skills workshop. 5:30–7:30pm
venue: Google Sydney HQ, 48 Pirrama Road, Pyrmont

speakers.name: David Brudenell (Co-CEO and Executive Chair, Decidr

title: Parramatta Pitch Night x A-One
description: A low-pressure pitch night in Western Sydney. Five to seven pitchers get three minutes each, then three minutes of questions and feedback from a judging panel, and the winner takes a $200 voucher. You do not need a registered company or a polished deck, just an idea you want to talk about. Come to pitch or come to watch — founders, students, side-hustlers and anyone with a business idea. 5:30–8:00pm
venue: Launch Pad Parramatta, Level 1, 6 Hassall Street, Parramatta

title: The Inner Game of Success: Master Your Mindset, Energy and Performance
description: An interactive workshop exploring the mental and emotional habits that drive peak performance in business and life. Practical exercises for breaking through mental barriers, building confidence and creating momentum in both business and life. Evening

title: I2N Accelerator Investor Showcase
Improv for Innovators & Leaders: Break Patterns. Spark New Ideas.
description: Improvisation as a working tool for founders: breaking a fixed pattern, thinking on your feet and getting comfortable being wrong in public. 6:00–9:00pm SS
venue: City of Sydney Creative Studios, 119 Bathurst Street, Sydney

title: Late Night Cafe
description: House party meets late-night cafe: founders and students in one room over good food and real conversation. Founders meet peers, potential hires and collaborators; students exploring tech get an honest look at the paths beyond a graduate program - founding, engineering, product and design. A potluck, so bring something if you can; brownies, matcha and coffee are already covered. 6:00–8:00pm

title: Navigating the Advisory Minefield
description: A panel on choosing and working with advisers, board members and investors: who actually helps, what good governance looks like early, and how to tell the difference before you hand over equity. 6:00–7:30pm
venue: Hall Chadwick, Level 40, 2 Park Street, Sydney

title: Pitching on Screen with Genevieve
description: How your presence reads on camera, and what to do about it, for founders who pitch over video as often as they pitch in a room. Ninety minutes of voice work, movement and play, putting the two together, and then demonstrations on screen. Bring a two-minute pitch or piece to camera if you can - five people drawn on the day get recorded feedback and media training from Genevieve afterwards.

title: Coffee Hour
description: A casual drop-in for people building, backing and supporting startups around Tech Central. No panels and no networking theatre - just coffee, conversation and the useful collisions that happen when founders, builders, investors and operators are in the same room. UTS Startups run it fortnightly; this one falls in festival week. Come for a quick cup or stay the hour. 10:00–11:30am

title: Interactive Design: Turn Your Value Proposition into an Experience
host: Utopia Rising with Western Sydney Startup Hub
description: A workshop on turning a value proposition into something people can see, feel, test and remember rather than sit through. Attendees prototype a demonstration of their own, which works as well for a personal brand or a room full of strangers as it does for a startup. 11:00am–12:00pm
venue: Western Sydney Startup Hub, North Parramatta

title: Humaning is your Moat: B2B Sales in the Age of AI
description: As AI becomes part of everyday business, the thing it still cannot do is be human, and that is your moat. A practical session on leaning into that alongside your AI tools so the connection that drives sales does not get lost. 11:00am–12:00pm CA

title: What do you do when your AI tells you no?
description: There is a difference between using AI as a tool and handing it a job it can refuse. The seven levels of AI maturity and which rung your business is actually on, agentic AI doing real work when it is briefed properly, and what it looks like when the AI says no - watched live, plus how to build the guardrails that let it. Cassandra took her own agency from fourteen people to four by building the systems instead of hiring. Capped at 40. 12:00–1:00pm
venue: Stone & Chalk Tech Central, Level 1, 477 Pitt Street, Haymarket

speakers.name: Cassandra Cadorin (Founder, CanTicket and House of Can

title: Demystifying Term Sheets
description: A practical workshop that takes the mystery out of term sheets and the part they play in early-stage investment. Richard Dale covers what a term sheet actually is, why one is used at all when it is not legally binding, the terms that turn up again and again and the reasons they are there, and how the document changes shape across different kinds of raise. Built for founders preparing to raise and for people new to investing, and followed by open Q&A. 12:30–1:15pm

title: Don’t Let Compliance Kill Your Sustainability Story
description: Sustainability communications are being squeezed from three sides at once: what audiences care about has shifted, regulators have tightened up, and AI search has changed how claims get found. A practitioner's session on treating compliance as a creative guardrail rather than a blocker - turning legal requirements into a stronger message, and making specific, evidence-backed claims that hold up and get found. Real cases, and questions at the end. 1:00–2:00pm

title: Angel Investing 101
description: For anyone curious about angel investing, and for founders who want to understand what the investor on the other side of the table is actually looking at. Philip Argy introduces the startup funding landscape, Australia's technology success stories and the early-stage ecosystem, then walks through what angel investing involves, the private capital journey, and how the Sydney Angels investment process works in practice. 1:00–4:00pm

title: Bushwalk with SquareBySquare
description: A bushwalk from Waverton Park to Balls Head Reserve, ending with a private heritage tour at the Coal Loader Centre for Sustainability. Being out in nature is a good way to close out a festival week: walking and talking beats sitting in rows, and it makes for a low-key networking session before people head off for a drink. Along the way, Henk and Emely share how SquareBySquare is building an economic model to fund nature conservation, using their own startup as a live case study of what it takes to make conservation work as a B2C business. 1:00–2:00pm BR
venue: Waverton Park to Balls Head Reserve — meet at the bus stop by Waverton Bowling Club, Woolcott Street

speakers.name: Henk Kleynhans and Emely Junker (Co-Founders, SquareBySquare

title: Hiring your first GTM or commercial lead
description: The first commercial hire is the one founders most often get wrong. What the role actually needs to cover at this stage, how to tell a closer from a builder, and what it costs to find out late. 6:30pm
venue: Stone & Chalk Tech Central, Level 1, 477 Pitt Street, Haymarket

title: Spark Festival 2026 Closing Celebration
description: The festival closes with the community that made it. Spark Foundation CEO Harry Godber and Simon Thomsen, editor of Startup Daily, are joined by the Hon. Paul Fletcher on the state of technology policy in Australia and what founders need to know about dealing with — and selling to — government.

speakers.name: The Hon. Paul Fletcher
speakers.role: Non-Executive Director, Tech Council of Australia

title: Spark AI Dinner
description: A dinner for founders, operators and investors working at the front edge of AI in Australia, closing out festival week over one table and one conversation.  Closing celebration
